instructions: Wash the parsley, mint and scallions and pat them dry. Finely chop 1/4 cup of the parsley, 2 tbsp of the mint and 2 of the scallions.
Crack the 6 eggs into a large bowl and whisk until smooth. Whisk in the flour, baking powder, allspice, salt and pepper until there are only a few small lumps left.
Stir in the parsley, mint and scallions.
Heat an 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tsp of the olive oil and wait until it shimmers.
Pour in about 1/2 cup of the batter and tilt the pan so it spreads into an even layer. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the top is mostly set.
Flip it and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's golden and set all the way through. Fold it in half and transfer it to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining oil and batter, 1 tsp of oil for each, to make 4 omelettes in all.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet or the microwave until they're soft.
Spread 1/4 cup of the yogurt over each pita. Unfold an omelette, lay it on the yogurt and roll the pita up around it.
Serve the rolls while they're warm.
method_notes: Every version whisks eggs with chopped herbs, a spoonful or two of flour and a pinch of baking powder and seven spice, then cooks them as thin omelettes or small fritters. No version has a rating of 4.0 or more from 20 or more people, so the lead is a fallback, and the app's rule picks Cosette's Kitchen (5 from 1 review, using the visible rating) for its herbs: parsley, mint and scallions. The batter ratios and the thin omelette method follow Amy's Dish (3.9 from 60 reviews, using the review count), cut from 8 omelettes to 4, since Cosette's makes thick fritters in a lot of oil. Ground allspice stands in for seven spice, as Cosette's suggests, and the zucchini is left out.
